llm.value: comparison of skeletal muscle proteome across four levels of physical activity (not active, active, moderately active, and highly active)
llm.evidence: To determine the effect of physical activity on the skeletal muscle proteome, we utilized liquid-chromatography mass spectrometry to obtain quantitative proteomics data on human skeletal muscle biopsies from 60 well-characterized healthy individuals (20–87 years) who reported heterogeneous levels of physical activity (not active, active, moderately active, and highly active).
Therefore, data from 58 participants dispersed over a wide age-range (20–34 years, n = 13; 35–49 years, n = 11; 50–64 years, n = 12; 65–79 years, n = 12; 80+ years, n = 10) were used for this study.
